title: China and Japan: Still Arguing, But Still (Mostly) Trading - The Wire China
gist: Ten months into what observers call the worst China-Japan diplomatic crisis in decades, the economic picture is split: bilateral trade is still growing while Chinese sanctions have hit a handful of key Japanese sectors hard, with no Takaichi-Xi summit since October 31, 2025.

insights.claim: Japan and China are ten months into what many observers describe as their worst diplomatic crisis in decades, yet bilateral trade between the two economies is still growing.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Political rupture is not translating into aggregate trade decoupling — headline diplomatic risk premia on Japan-China exposed names may be overstated relative to actual flows.

insights.claim: Chinese sanctions in the dispute have been narrowly targeted, hitting a handful of key sectors hard rather than suppressing overall bilateral commerce.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Beijing's playbook is sector-surgical coercion, so the trade is to underweight the specific sanctioned sectors rather than broad Japan exposure.
insights.locator: Ten months in, the picture for economic ties

insights.claim: The last high-profile summit between Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Xi Jinping was held on October 31, 2025 on the sidelines of the APEC leaders' meeting in Gyeongju, South Korea, and none has followed.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: The absence of leader-level contact for ten months is the cleanest observable gauge of de-escalation odds; a scheduled summit would be the signal to fade sanctioned-sector discounts.
